title: Income Records Due Date for Long-Term Hardship Hold Reviews: Calculation Clause
content:
**Clause.** Under Hardship and Protective Holds, the updated household income records requested for a status review of a running Long-Term Hardship Hold are due on the last day of the upcoming status review's overdue window: the days allowed for the income records run from the day of the request to the due date of the status review that next falls due, reviews falling due every review interval counted from the hold's start date, plus the tier's review overdue days. A status review falling due on the day of the request counts as already fallen due, so the review that next falls due is the following one. The income records due date never falls after the hold's current end date: where the count would carry it past that date, the due date is the hold's current end date and the days allowed are the days from the request to it. The days allowed for the income records are a whole number of calendar days and are not rounded.

## Inputs

| Input | Source |
|---|---|
| The hold's start date and current end date | The hold's record |
| Review interval and review overdue days | The Long-Term Hardship Hold's figures in the product's status review calendar |
| The day of the request | The day the request is made |

## Worked examples (hypothetical; review interval 60 days, overdue days 15, as the calendar sets for this tier)

Start date 1 March, so reviews fall due on 30 April, 29 June and 28 August.

**A. Request on 20 June, current end date 27 August.** The next review falls due on 29 June, 9 days after the request. Days allowed: 9 plus 15, that is 24; due date 14 July, which is before 27 August, so 24 stands.

**B. Request on 20 June, current end date 5 July.** The same count of 24 would carry the due date to 14 July, after 5 July. The due date is 5 July and the days allowed are 15.
